tools.name: get_overview
tools.description: Today at a glance: scheduled split, readiness, the least-recovered muscles, this week's counts, streak, an active lighter week or today's adjustment, days since the last session. Call it first when a question is about today or 'how am I doing'.

tools.name: get_sessions
tools.description: List logged sessions (newest first) with day, split, duration, set count and top lifts. Use it to find a session id or to see what was trained when.

tools.name: get_session
tools.description: Every set of one session (load, reps, effort, flags), its post-session notes, and a heart summary when health sharing is on. Use after get_sessions.

tools.name: get_exercise_history
tools.description: Per-session history of one exercise, newest session first: top set, strength estimate (e1RM), effort mix; plus plateau status, trend, records and effort drift. Call it for any question about progress, stalls or a specific lift.

exerciseId.description: An exercise id from search_exercises or get_plan, e.g. lib_barbell_bench_press.

tools.name: get_next_target
tools.description: The app's next-session target for an exercise (load, reps, reason, confidence), snapped to the equipment's loads, with a warm-up ramp and the primary muscles' recovery. Use for 'what should I lift'.

exerciseId.description: An exercise id from search_exercises or get_plan, e.g. lib_barbell_bench_press.

tools.name: get_recovery
tools.description: Recovery per muscle: percent, hours until ready, when fully recovered, top drivers and confidence. Pass `at` (ISO, up to 7 days ahead) to project. `soreToday` marks a muscle that today's soreness rating alone is holding back, past what the model's clock would otherwise say; hoursLeft and fullInHours are null there rather than a misleading 0. Use for soreness, readiness to train a muscle, or scheduling.

at.description: Optional ISO time, up to 7 days ahead.

tools.name: get_readiness
tools.description: Today's (or a past day's) readiness: score, band, drivers, load advice, confidence, the baselines it compares against, and optionally the band for recent days. Use for 'why am I amber/red' or 'should I train hard'.

tools.name: get_volume
tools.description: Weekly effective sets per muscle against the person's volume band, with the 4-week median, plus weekly totals. Use for volume, balance or 'am I doing enough'.

tools.name: get_records
tools.description: Personal records, newest first, optionally for one exercise.

exerciseId.description: An exercise id from search_exercises or get_plan, e.g. lib_barbell_bench_press.

tools.name: get_insights
tools.description: Every current coach insight (not just the top three) with id, category, priority, title, what was noticed, what it means, the action and its numbers; the weekly review; and whether a lighter week is due. Prefer this over guessing what matters.

tools.name: get_plan
tools.description: The goal (rep ranges, effort target, rest), every split with exercises and sets, the weekly schedule, reminders, rest mode, an active lighter week and today’s adjustment. Call before proposing any change to splits or the schedule.

tools.name: get_body
tools.description: Weight trend (kg/week and % per week), latest weight, body-fat readings and BMI. Needs body sharing.

tools.name: get_health
tools.description: Daily sleep, resting heart rate, steps and active calories from Health Connect. Needs health sharing.

tools.name: get_heart_session
tools.description: One session's heart data: time in zones, per-set peaks, rest recovery, drift and effort mismatch. Needs health sharing.

tools.name: get_live_session
tools.description: The session in progress: split, elapsed time, current exercise, sets done vs planned, rest timer, the in-session adjustment, and live heart-rate freshness. Call first in live mode.

tools.name: search_exercises
tools.description: Find exercises by name, muscle, equipment or movement pattern. Use to get exercise ids before proposing splits or swaps.

tools.name: get_exercise
tools.description: Full details of one exercise: muscles, equipment, pattern, type, role, up to 6 substitutes and a coaching cue.

exerciseId.description: An exercise id from search_exercises or get_plan, e.g. lib_barbell_bench_press.

tools.name: get_equipment
tools.description: The equipment profile for an exercise at a gym (entry unit, steps, dumbbell ladder, bar, plates), the active gym, and loadable neighbours of the current target. Use before talking about loads in lb or kg, plates or dumbbell jumps.

exerciseId.description: An exercise id from search_exercises or get_plan, e.g. lib_barbell_bench_press.

tools.name: find_in_app
tools.description: Search the app itself: returns the 5 best screens, panels or actions with where they are and how to use them. Use when unsure where something lives.

query.description: What the person wants to find or do.

tools.name: explain_method
tools.description: How the app computes a number (recovery, readiness, progression, volume bands and more), its constants and this person's own calibration values. Use for any 'how is X calculated' or 'why does the app say'.

tools.name: lookup_knowledge
tools.description: Evidence cards on training, recovery, sleep and nutrition basics, with key numbers. Required before stating any general number; cite the card as ⟦k:id⟧.

tools.name: calculate
tools.description: Arithmetic on the person’s numbers. Never compute in your head: use this for BMI, e1RM, loads for reps, percent change, unit conversion, plates, weekly rate, protein range and days between dates.

barKg.description: Bar weight in kg; default from the gym.

exerciseId.description: An exercise id from search_exercises or get_plan, e.g. lib_barbell_bench_press.

tools.name: propose_reminder

tools.name: propose_setting
tools.description: Propose changing one app setting: rest mode, automatic rest, rest length, display unit, the daily quote or haptics.

tools.name: snooze_insight
tools.description: Mark an insight helpful or snooze it for 7 days, when the person says so. Applied at once with Undo.

tools.name: propose_equipment_profile
tools.description: Propose how a piece of equipment loads at a gym (unit, steps, dumbbell ladder, bar, plates), e.g. from a rack photo or "the dumbbells here are in pounds". If unsure of the unit, ask one question first.

exerciseId.description: An exercise id from search_exercises or get_plan, e.g. lib_barbell_bench_press.

step.description: Smallest jump in the unit, above 0.

ladder.description: Available loads in the unit, ascending, at most 80.

addOns.description: Stack add-on weights in the unit.

plates.description: Plate sizes per side, in the unit.

tools.name: propose_gym
tools.description: Propose adding a gym and making it the active one.

tools.name: escalate
tools.description: Show the app’s fixed safety card: pain (sharp, spreading, numb, or lasting past 48 h), medical (chest pain, fainting, dizziness), crisis, or disordered eating. Always use it in those situations.

tools.name: remember
tools.description: Remember a durable fact the person stated (injury, equipment, preference, goal in their words, agreement). Written at once with Undo. Not for feelings or one-offs.

tools.name: forget
tools.description: Forget one memory item when the person asks.

tools.name: recall
tools.description: Look up remembered items beyond the 12 in the brief.

modes.chat: Conversation. At most 120 words unless they ask for depth.
modes.plan: Design mode. Ask at most 2 clarifying questions (days/week, session length, equipment, priorities) unless memory answers them. Draft → evaluate_plan → revise → show(plan_week) + show(plan_evaluation) → propose_program.
modes.live: They're mid-workout. At most 40 words. Use get_live_session first. Offer at most one adjustment via propose_today.
modes.brief: Write today's brief: one headline (at most 90 characters) and up to 3 priorities, each tied to an insight id from get_insights, in your words (at most 140 characters each). Use read tools if needed. Never invent insights.
modes.moment: Write one line (at most 140 characters) for this moment from the facts given, plus up to 2 follow-up chips. Numbers only from the facts.
modes.summarize: Summarise this conversation: a title (at most 40 characters), an episode (at most 200 characters, plain words, what was discussed and agreed), and up to 3 durable facts worth remembering (kind + text).
